$comment:
JSON-image case table, shared byte-for-byte by the three engines that turn a caller value into
JSON text on the wire: openbindings-go/formats/openapi, openapi-client/go, and
openapi-client/typescript/src (which openbindings-ts/packages/openapi re-exports). Each case is
rendered as a WHOLE OpenAPI document and loaded through each engine's own shipped loader, so the
table exercises the shipped path rather than a hand-built typed model.

THE QUESTION. RFC 8259 Section 7 requires exactly three escapes inside a JSON string --
"quotation mark, reverse solidus, and the control characters (U+0000 through U+001F)" -- and then
permits, but never requires, any other character to be escaped: "Any character may be escaped."
AMPERSAND (U+0026), LESS-THAN SIGN (U+003C) and GREATER-THAN SIGN (U+003E) all fall inside the
`unescaped = %x20-21 / %x23-5B / %x5D-10FFFF` production, so both spellings are conformant and
neither is required. Read at the pinned bytes: corpus-lab authority pin
authorities/texts/openapi/json/rfc8259.txt, SHA-256
61a5378f4255c720beb2a4b4a63b29540147c140f36988bf086291989b4cd2d7.

An implementation must still put ONE byte string on the wire, so the choice is neither the
incorporated authority's nor openbindings.openapi@1's -- its Section 10 places document
translation outside the specification. It is THE IMPLEMENTATIONS' CONVENTION, stated in
openapi-client/go/json_image.go, openbindings-go/formats/openapi/json_image.go and
openapi-client/typescript/src/json-image.ts: EMIT THE LITERAL CHARACTERS. Go's encoding/json
escapes all three by default so its output is safe to embed in HTML; no lane here embeds JSON in
HTML, so the two Go engines disable that escape explicitly rather than inheriting it.

HOW THE EXPECTATIONS WERE AUTHORED. Never by reading an engine. Three rules compose:
  (1) the JSON image -- RFC 8259 Section 7 plus the convention above (literal characters);
  (2) the CONTENT-lane form escaper -- RFC 1866 Section 8.2.1 / RFC 1738 Section 2.2, emitted as
      the WHATWG form-urlencoded serializer set (see testdata/urlencoded-escaper-cases.json,
      whose audit this table does not reopen);
  (3) the STYLE-lane escaper -- RFC 6570 with allowReserved not in effect, so RFC 3986's
      unreserved set and %20 for a space.

THE STYLE LANE IS THE CONTROL. The two urlencoded lanes are SUPPOSED to differ (a space is `+` on
the content lane and %20 on the style lane) and that partition is audited and closed. The style
lane never forms a JSON image at all, so its cells must be byte-identical before and after this
convergence; a fix that leaked across the lanes would move them.

Every value is a SINGLE-KEY object so member ordering never enters the table: Go sorts a map's
keys and JavaScript preserves insertion order, and a twin table must not pin a difference it is
not about. The `none` cell carries no character of the class and is the second control.

cases.name: 3.0.3|urlencoded-style|none
cases.basis: The style lane never forms a JSON image at all — form/explode=true expands the object's members as separate name=value pairs and each is escaped by rule 3. These cells are the CONTROL: they must be byte-identical before and after the convergence, and an implementation that converged the two lanes would break them.
